newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestine stock exchange opens on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Palestine stock exchange opens on Tuesday.

text.p: The first Palestinian stock market opens in the West Bank town of Nablus on Tuesday with limited trading to start but plans to add sessions as volume increase.

In a statement on Monday the Palestine Securities Exchange (PSE) said it would kick off with one trading session per week "marking the end of the developmental stage of the exchange and the begining of a one-month introductory phase of trading".
"Regularly-scheduled trading with multiple sessions per week is expected to be added as trading volume warrants it," the statement said.

Traders were opening accounts for investors as PSE officials made final preparations on Monday for the opening. Officials said the bourse will open at 10:00 local time (0800 GMT) and close at 1330 (1130 GMT).

Officials who oversaw the establishment of the $2 million fully-automated bourse said the exchange was intended to encourage expatriate Palestinians to invest in their country without having to come back.
They said trading would be carried out by traders from their offices and that the exchange was designed to provide maximum security to investors.

The PSE statement said 23 companies had been listed on the exchange and that 20 other companies are expected to complete listing procedures by the end of the introductory phase. It said that 60 public share-holding companies are eligible to be listed, with an estimated capitalisation of $700 million to be listed.
Four brokerage firms were also registered in the exchange and traders and brokers have undergone intensive training at the bourse.
Jiriyes Qassis, general manager of the Ramallah-based United Securities Company, said he expected betwen 5,000 and 10,000 shares to be traded on the first day of trading.

"I think that with the successful opening and eventually successful trading and the build up of volume, the stock exchange will be a venue to create liquidity and to re-invest in Palestine thus creating more job opportunities and more flourishment for our economy," Qassis said.
The exchange signed an agreement with the Jordan-based Arab Bank to act as a clearinghouse.
